script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Wednesday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed three point zero nine percent down on the session.

Micron Technology fell nearly ten percent on Wednesday. That single move erased meaningful ground across the semiconductor complex, and it did not fall alone.

The broad market took a significant hit on Wednesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped over eleven hundred points as sinking technology stocks collided with a sharp rise in oil prices, pulling the S&P 500 down one point five percent. The Nasdaq composite slumped one point seven percent, compounding pressure across this portfolio's technology-heavy positions.

Micron Technology was the sharpest wound in this portfolio on Wednesday, falling nine point nine four percent on the session. The move did not happen in isolation. Applied Materials dropped eight point four percent, and KLA Corporation — a secondary holding — shed an extraordinary ten point eight percent. Lam Research declined six point four percent. This was a coordinated selloff across semiconductor equipment and memory, not a stock-specific event. For Micron specifically, the backdrop is a memory market navigating supply-demand tension even as AI-driven demand narratives remain intact. Qualcomm separately reported a twenty percent drop in smartphone chip revenue and forecast weaker profits ahead, signaling that consumer-facing semiconductor demand remains uneven. For holders of Micron, the question now is whether the AI memory thesis absorbs this pressure or whether the next earnings cycle forces a reset.

NVIDIA fell three point five five percent on Wednesday. The company announced it has scheduled a conference call for its second-quarter financial results, with a written CFO commentary to be provided ahead of the call. That event is now the key near-term catalyst for the stock. Meanwhile, an ecosystem partner — Penguin Solutions — is up one hundred twenty-three percent in 2026, with its chief executive arguing the real bottleneck in AI infrastructure is not GPUs but memory and system integration. That framing matters for how this portfolio's largest holding gets valued going forward.

Apple slipped zero point five six percent on Wednesday, narrowly missing the five trillion dollar market capitalization milestone, snapping a three-day winning streak in the process. Qualcomm's earnings added a notable wrinkle — the chipmaker said Apple-related revenue would decline faster than expected due to supply constraints and rising costs across the supply chain. Qualcomm plans to raise prices beginning September first. Apple reports its fiscal third-quarter earnings after the closing bell on Thursday.

Alphabet rose zero point nine zero percent on Wednesday, making it one of the few primary holdings to close in positive territory. A Seeking Alpha analysis flagged that while the broader selloff overshadowed the story, Alphabet's second-quarter results showed cloud revenue up eighty-two percent and Search revenue up seventeen percent, with its AI Mode product reaching one billion monthly active users. Free cash flow dipped as capital expenditure rose. Waymo also added an undisclosed passenger experience feature, signaling continued competitive investment in autonomous ride-hailing.

Turning to Microsoft, the stock slipped zero point seven one percent on the session, even as separate coverage noted the company's strong cloud and software performance is driving it up five point five percent over the past month. Over at Amazon, shares fell one point eight two percent, underperforming the broader index on a difficult tape for consumer discretionary and cloud names alike.

Advanced Micro Devices dropped five point five one percent on Wednesday, tracking the broader semiconductor decline closely. No company-specific catalyst emerged, but the move aligns with the sector-wide pressure seen across chipmakers. Intel fell five point one two percent, also moving with the semiconductor complex in a session defined by weakness across the group.

Tesla declined two point nine seven percent on Wednesday, consistent with the broader consumer discretionary selloff. No earnings catalyst is imminent, but the stock continues to trade with sensitivity to broader risk appetite.

Meanwhile, Meta Platforms — a secondary holding worth noting — fell one point three one percent after a D.A. Davidson analyst described the company's revenue forecast as, quote, barely passable. That language from a technology sector research head carries weight heading into the next phase of the earnings cycle.

Three data points demand attention in the next forty-eight hours. First, Apple reports fiscal third-quarter earnings after the close on Thursday, July thirtieth — the single most important near-term event for a holding that represents six point eight percent of this portfolio. Second, NVIDIA's scheduled earnings call and advance CFO commentary represent the highest-weight catalyst in the portfolio — timing to be confirmed, but proximity to August makes this imminent. Third, watch for any Federal Reserve commentary following Wednesday's session, as rate policy sensitivity remains elevated across this portfolio's technology concentration.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Apple earnings after Thursday's close will set the tone for the entire technology complex — that print is the one to watch.
